data.title: Engineering Manager- Linux & Kernel
data.description:
Hungry, Humble, Honest, with Heart. 

The Opportunity

Nutanix AHV builds on top of the open-source x86-KVM stack, with an emphasis on performance, scale, and reliability. The hyperconverged nature of our stack provides the phenomenal potential for optimizations cutting across various parts of our stack -- right from the kernel and ranging up to, but not limited by, the management layer. 

We are looking for original thinkers who won't hesitate to demand conventional thought in arriving at out-of-the-box solutions. 

We aim to work as closely aligned with the open-source community as possible. Our engineers are highly encouraged to participate in open-source community development. Any work you do will be preserved as open-source commit(s) for posterity!

A day in the life of an AHV hypervisor engineer: 

- Problems you'll solve: 
 - We've always believed in demanding the status quo and disrupting ourselves to provide the best in-class customer experience. A case in point: Nutanix is well known for providing a zero-touch upgrade experience for our customers. Within the hypervisor team, we are focussing on various ways to make this faster and more reliable -- by pushing the limits of VM live migrations towards speed and predictability, or rethinking why a hypervisor upgrade should need a reboot at all. 
About The Team

At Nutanix, you will have the opportunity to be part of the Hypervisor team, a dynamic group that is spread out geographically. Despite being in different locations, the team collaborates effectively and maintains a strong sense of camaraderie. Working with the Hypervisor team means being surrounded by talented people who are supportive, making it a great team to work with. This setup also provides exciting exposure to diverse perspectives and opportunities for personal and professional growth. 

You will report to a Senior Manager who is committed to supporting your development and ensuring your success within the organization. This role operates in a hybrid capacity, blending the benefits of remote work with the advantages of in-person collaboration. In locations where our workplace policy applies (i. e. San Jose, Durham, Mexico City, Bangalore, Pune, Hoofddorp, Belgrade, Barcelona, Singapore, Sydney and Tokyo), employees are expected to work onsite a minimum of 3 days per week to foster collaboration, team alignment, and access to in-office resources. Workplace type may vary based on location and team requirements. Please speak with your recruiter for details. Additional team-specific guidance and norms will be provided by your manager. As for travel requirements, there are none, allowing you to focus on your projects without the need for frequent travel. 

Your Role

Role

You'll be managing a team of extremely talented engineers across a spectrum of geographies and experience. The most successful candidate for this role will be someone who can: 

- Constantly look for ways to improve the product, learning from customer questions and not limited to existing technologies. 
 - Devise solutions and back them up with solid research and numbers to prove their efficacy. 
 - Have the ability to convey ideas to a geographically diverse audience using excellent communication/writing skills. 
 - Participate in design discussions, often outside one's known comfort zone -- learning on the go. 
 - Proactively mentor junior members of the team, finding ways to fuel their intelligent curiosity and leverage their unique strengths. 
 - Not hesitate to help out with occasional customer escalations: Nutanix believes in putting customers first. While we have a huge, dedicated team to assist customers with any issues, there might be situations where engineering help might be sought to bail out a rare, unfortunate outage. 
 - Take pride in working with open-source communities to fold product improvements back into community projects. 

What You Will Bring

- The must-haves: 
 - Rock-solid OS/systems fundamentals drive design and implementation. 
 - Low-level coding and debugging experience with at least one hardware architecture, preferably x86. 
 - The ability to write and maintain enterprise-quality code. 
 - Deep reasoning and detailed skills, which provide top-down thinking to break down abstract concepts into actionable pieces. 
 - Proven feature delivery experience: should have 8+ years of hands-on experience of what it means to ship enterprise-quality code to customers. 
 - The good-to-haves: 
 - Knowledge of x86 virtualization and the KVM stack. 
 - Code contributions to the Linux kernel/virtualization stack is an added plus. 
Desired Qualification & Experience

- Bachelor's/Master's degree in computer science or equivalent. 
 - 12+ years of experience building enterprise-grade software, preferably some with guide experience. 

--

data.title: AI Engineering Lead
data.description:
Role Overview: 

We are looking for an AI-first Engineering Lead to build and run a high-output engineering team. The team is responsible for customized client development, independent technology projects and workflow automation. 

This is not a conventional engineering management role where AI is used only as a productivity tool. The entire mandate is built around an AI-native engineering model. 

AI agents, coding copilots, automated testing, AI-assisted code review, documentation generation, debugging and workflow automation should become the default way the team operates. 

You will lead a team of approximately 7-10 engineers and QA resources and deliver approximately 3-5 new customized projects or programs every month, while also supporting existing enterprise applications. 

The core objective is: 

Use AI to materially increase engineering output, reduce repetitive manual work and create a predictable, high-quality customization and project-delivery engine. 

Business Context: 

We build and operate enterprise Loyalty, Promotions, Rewards and Engagement platforms for large brands. Our core platform supports common functionality, but enterprise clients regularly require: 

- Additional workflows
 - Client-specific business logic
 - Integrations
 - New modules
 - Custom interfaces
 - Special reporting
 - Independent applications
 - New digital experiences
 - Functionality not yet available in the standard platformThe Engineering Lead will own the engineering function responsible for delivering these requirements. The role will also take over a substantial part of the technology responsibility that currently depends on individual knowledge holders. 

AI-First Engineering Mandate: 

The most important part of this role is the ability to redesign how engineering work gets done. We want the development lifecycle to increasingly operate through the following flow: 

Requirement → AI-assisted analysis → Solution design → Agentic development → Automated testing → AI-assisted review → Deployment → Monitoring → AI-assisted support

The Engineering Lead will create workflows where AI handles as much repeatable engineering work as safely possible. This includes: 

- Legacy code understanding
 - Codebase navigation
 - Dependency mapping
 - Impact analysis
 - Code generation
 - Repetitive customization development
 - API scaffolding
 - Refactoring
 - Migration scripts
 - Automated test generation
 - Regression automation
 - Code review
 - Documentation
 - Security analysis
 - Debugging
 - Incident diagnosis
 - Production support assistanceTools may include: 

- Cursor
 - Claude
 - Copilot
 - AI coding agents
 - Workflow automation tools
 - LLM-based internal engineering agents
 - Automated testing and review systemsThe ideal candidate should be able to move beyond simple "AI-assisted coding" into AI-orchestrated engineering workflows. 

Workflow Automation: 

You will identify repetitive engineering and operational workflows that can be automated. Examples include: 

- Requirement interpretation
 - Technical estimation
 - Test case preparation
 - Release readiness checks
 - Deployment validation
 - Log analysis
 - Incident triage
 - Documentation updates
 - Change impact analysis
 - Support diagnostics
 - Repetitive client customization workAI and automation should progressively reduce the manual effort required across the full software delivery lifecycle. 

Customized Client Development: 

The team will own all engineering requirements that fall outside the standard capabilities of the core platform. For every requirement, the Engineering Lead must decide whether it should be: 

- Handled through configuration
 - Developed once as a reusable platform capability
 - Built as a controlled customization
 - Delivered as a separate, independent application

The Engineering Lead will own: 

- Requirement understanding
 - Technical solutioning
 - Architecture
 - Estimation
 - Sprint planning
 - Resource allocation
 - Development
 - Code review
 - QA
 - Deployment
 - Production stabilizationMultiple client projects will run in parallel. 

Independent Projects: 

The team will also deliver technology projects that may sit outside the existing core platform. These may include: 

- Client portals
 - Workflow applications
 - Microsites
 - API integrations
 - Dashboards
 - Campaign technologies
 - Automation tools
 - Internal productivity systems
 - Experimental productsThe Engineering Lead should be comfortable choosing the right architecture and stack instead of forcing every requirement into the existing monolith. 

Current Technology Environment: 

The current platform includes: 

- PHP / Yii
 - Angular
 - Ionic / mobile components
 - PostgreSQL
 - APIs and third-party integrations
 - Queue and asynchronous processing
 - Enterprise client applications
 - A largely monolithic architecture
 - Multiple historic client-specific customizationsThe environment is being modernized progressively. The person joining must be comfortable working with an existing monolith, improving it pragmatically, and using AI to understand and extend it efficiently. This is not a greenfield-only role. 

Team Leadership: 

The Engineering Lead will manage approximately 7-10 engineers, QA and technical resources and will be expected to actively drive: 

- Engineering productivity
 - Sprint planning
 - Resource allocation
 - Delivery commitments
 - Technical reviews
 - Architecture
 - Code quality
 - QA quality
 - Production readiness
 - AI adoption
 - Workflow automation
 - Individual accountabilityThe person must stay close enough to the work to know: 

- What each engineer is building
 - Where delivery is blocked
 - Where AI can replace repetitive work
 - Where quality is weak
 - Where architectural decisions need intervention

Engineering Quality & Architecture: 

The Engineering Lead will be accountable for: 

- Architecture decisions
 - Reusable components
 - API design
 - Database design
 - Security
 - Scalability
 - Performance
 - Code standards
 - Technical debt
 - CI/CD
 - Production reliabilityThe person must ensure that short-term custom requirements do not create long-term fragmentation. A key principle is: 

Build once where possible, configure repeatedly, customize only where necessary. 

Quality & Delivery Discipline: 

You will establish a disciplined delivery model covering: 

- Scope clarity
 - Estimation
 - Sprint execution
 - Code review
 - Automated testing
 - Regression
 - QA gates
 - Release checklists
 - Deployment
 - Rollback
 - Incident management
 - Root cause analysis (RCA)
 - Production monitoring

What We Are Looking For: 

We are specifically looking for someone who: 

- Thinks AI-first rather than traditional-development-first
 - Has strong hands-on engineering depth
 - Can manage a team of 7-10 people
 - Can architect and review systems
 - Is highly comfortable with legacy and monolithic applications
 - Can run multiple client projects simultaneously
 - Understands AI coding tools deeply
 - Can design agentic engineering workflows
 - Can automate repetitive development and support processes
 - Can balance speed, quality and business deadlines
 - Is strong in debugging and production problem-solving
 - Can challenge weak engineering practices
 - Can improve engineering output per person

Relevant Experience: 

Ideally, the candidate will have: 

- 10-15+ years of software engineering experience
 - 3-5+ years in engineering leadership
 - Experience managing teams of 7-15 people
 - Strong backend and API architecture skills
 - Experience in PHP / Yii / Laravel or similar frameworks (preferred)
 - Angular or modern frontend exposure
 - PostgreSQL or other relational database experience
 - CI/CD and production engineering experience
 - Enterprise integration experience
 - Legacy modernization experience
 - Strong hands-on use of Cursor, Claude, Copilot or equivalent tools
 - Experience building AI-assisted or agentic development workflows

data.title: Staff Site Reliability Engineer, Environment Automation
data.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. 

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. 

- Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. 

As a Staff Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) at GitLab, you'll help keep all user-facing services and production systems reliable, scalable, and efficient. Our SREs combine a pragmatic operations mindset with strong software engineering practices to drive automation, reduce toil, and improve resilience across our platform. 

In the Environment Automation specialization, your focus is on operating and automating hundreds of GitLab environments-from initial provisioning to day-to-day maintenance tasks. 

Unlike other SRE roles, this position centers on automating the lifecycle of many tenant environments, ensuring they remain secure, consistent, and reliable at scale. 

Some Examples Of The Projects You Could Work On

- Designing infrastructure automation that provisions and operates GitLab environments using Terraform, Ansible, and Kubernetes
 - Creating and maintaining deployment packages for GitLab, such as Helm Charts and omnibus-gitlab
 - Building and operating Dedicated GitLab instances integrated with cloud-native services (e. g. , GCP, AWS)
 - Developing tools to orchestrate infrastructure-as-code workflows across multiple tenants
 - Deploying and managing microservices on Kubernetes clusters at scale
 - Enhancing GitLab's observability stack (e. g. , Prometheus, ELK) to support proactive monitoring and incident response
 - Integrating with and operating infrastructure in cloud provider ecosystems (e. g. , IAM, networking, storage)
 - Championing and implementing cloud security best practices across automated infrastructure

What You'll Do

- Build & Scale Multi-Tenant Infrastructure: Design and implement automation that provisions and manages hundreds of isolated GitLab environments using Terraform, Ansible, and Kubernetes. Manage complex state strategies and workspace configurations to support scale and maintainability. 
 - Debug & Resolve Production Issues: Troubleshoot issues across Kubernetes clusters, cloud services, and GitLab apps-identifying root causes of failed deployments, crash loops, and scheduling conflicts to ensure service continuity. 
 - Automate Operations at Scale: Replace manual workflows with infrastructure-as-code solutions, including automated version upgrades, configuration rollouts, and provisioning pipelines that operate reliably across all tenants. 
 - Monitor & Predict Capacity: Build observability systems that detect bottlenecks, predict usage trends, and optimize resource consumption using tools like Prometheus, ELK, and Grafana. 
 - Respond & Lead During Incidents: Lead incident response and postmortem efforts, applying technical depth to resolve issues and establish operational standards that reduce future risk. 
 - Architect & Collaborate: Influence architectural decisions around automation, scalability, and operational excellence. Partner with engineering teams to improve automation, platform resilience, and production-readiness. 

What You'll Bring

- Production-Scale Experience: Proven ability to operate and troubleshoot production workloads across multiple tenants or environments. Deep understanding of how distributed systems fail at scale and how to build in resilience. Terraform & IaC Mastery: Strong hands-on experience with Terraform, including workspace strategies, state management, and automation patterns that scale. Comfortable solving state isolation issues and building reliable, reusable infrastructure code. Experience with Ansible and templating tools like Jsonnet is a plus. Kubernetes in Production: Skilled at diagnosing deployment failures, interpreting pod logs, and debugging scheduling issues and rollback scenarios in live environments. Understands how pods, ReplicaSets, and controllers interact in production. Programming & Code Analysis: Ability to read and debug code in Go and/or Ruby. Familiar with identifying performance issues, scalability concerns, and contributing to infrastructure tooling through thoughtful code analysis. Large Scale Operations Background: Experience supporting infrastructure for many customers or environments simultaneously. Comfortable managing isolation, scaling, monitoring, and incident response across diverse workloads. Architecture & Incident Response: Able to reason through complex systems and operational challenges. Brings on-call experience and can lead technical discussions and incident resolution efforts under pressure. Customer-Focused Collaboration: Proven ability to work across teams and with internal or external customers to solve technical problems while maintaining service commitments and clear communication. GitLab Platform Proficiency: Comfortable using GitLab as a daily tool for infrastructure automation, collaboration, and operational workflows. 

About The Team

GitLab's Dedicated team, where the SRE Environment Automation role sits, is on a mission to deliver a fully managed, single-tenant GitLab experience through the GitLab Dedicated platform. Our goal is to eliminate manual operations across the entire lifecycle of customer environments, including provisioning, upgrades, security, and monitoring, so customers can focus on unlocking the full potential of The One DevOps Platform without managing the underlying infrastructure. We build scalable, automated systems that ensure each GitLab Dedicated instance is secure, consistent, and production-ready-whether we're managing 10 environments or hundreds. 

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

- Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
 - Flexible Paid Time Off 
 - Team Member Resource Groups
 - Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
 - Growth and Development Fund
 - Parental Leave

Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application. 

Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process. 

Privacy Policy: Please review our Recruitment Privacy Policy. Your privacy is important to us. 

GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab's policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also GitLab's EEO Policy and EEO is the Law. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know during the recruiting process.

data.title: Team Lead, Product Operations,  Climate
data.description:
Job Purpose

ICE Climate Operations supports ICE's Climate Risk Data business, covering physical climate risk, transition risk, nature-related risk, and avoided emissions across public and private companies, sovereigns, and structured finance assets such as mortgage-backed and municipal securities. The Physical Risk team runs the geospatial research and quality assurance function behind this coverage, identifying and validating corporate and sovereign asset locations against wildfire, flood, hurricane, and extreme-temperature exposure for ICE's global geospatial risk platform. 

Lead the operational delivery and continuous improvement of Physical Risk data projects within ICE Climate Operations. The role manages and develops a team of analysts responsible for asset-location research, geospatial validation, structured quality assurance, and project delivery. It combines people leadership with hands-on oversight of complex research and QA, ensuring data is accurate, complete, traceable, and delivered in line with product and client priorities. 

The team leader is the primary operational contact for Physical Risk workstreams and coordinates closely with Product, R&D, Engineering, Analytics, and Data Quality teams. The role is expected to translate evolving requirements into clear work plans, maintain visibility of progress and risks, and build the team's ability to support product improvements and respond to data-related queries with increasing independence. 

Responsibilities

- Team leadership and delivery management
 - Lead, coach, and develop a team of associates and senior associates, setting clear expectations for delivery, quality, accountability, and professional growth. 
 - Convert business and project priorities into practical work plans, allocate resources across concurrent workstreams, and adjust assignments as priorities change. 
 - Monitor milestones, productivity, quality, and turnaround times; identify delivery risks early and implement recovery actions. 
 - Conduct regular one-to-one discussions, goal setting, performance reviews, and development planning; support recruitment, onboarding, and succession readiness. 
 - Act as the first point of escalation for operational blockers, quality concerns, scope ambiguity, and resourcing conflicts. 
 - Physical risk project and product support
 - Lead operational support for Physical Risk initiatives, including industrial and mine location QA, high-materiality asset review, corporate mapping, location weighting, and damage-function research across corporate, sovereign, and private-company asset classes. 
 - Coordinate delivery with Product and R&D stakeholders, clarify objectives and acceptance criteria, maintain project status and dependencies, and ensure outputs are usable for downstream product or model development. 
 - Keep the team focused on work that improves the quality and coverage of Physical Risk products, including continuous QA of critical asset data and on-demand QA or updates for client-driven requirements spanning wildfire, flood, hurricane, and extreme-temperature exposure. 
 - Build sufficient product and methodology knowledge within the team to support data samples, stakeholder queries, and issue investigation with reduced dependency on Product teams. 
 - Research, geospatial data, and quality assurance
 - Oversee research to identify, classify, map, and validate corporate asset locations, ownership relationships, operational status, facility type, coordinates, and materiality indicators. 
 - Ensure consistent use of authoritative internal data, third-party datasets, company disclosures, mapping platforms, satellite imagery, and documented public sources. 
 - Review complex or high-risk discrepancies, confirm source traceability, approve final outputs, and direct root-cause analysis and corrective actions. 
 - Oversee QA controls for completeness, coordinate accuracy, classification, duplication, status, source evidence, and conformity with approved methodologies and due-diligence standards. 
 - Ensure project outputs are documented, reproducible, and ready for ingestion, analytics, model research, or client delivery as applicable. 
 - Data, reporting, and operational governance
 - Use SQL and BigQuery to retrieve, join, analyze, and validate entity and location datasets; use advanced Excel and reporting tools to manage and communicate delivery performance. 
 - Maintain concise dashboards and status reporting covering scope, milestones, quality, throughput, risks, dependencies, and decisions required. 
 - Establish clear operating procedures, research playbooks, source hierarchies, QA checklists, and hand-off criteria; keep documentation current as requirements evolve. 
 - Support audits, internal reviews, release validation, production issue analysis, and governance activities relevant to Physical Risk data operations. 
 - Process improvement, automation, and capability building
 - Identify recurring data and workflow issues and implement scalable improvements that reduce manual effort, rework, and turnaround time without weakening control quality. 
 - Promote responsible use of AI-assisted research, automated validation, and smart workflows, with human verification and clear evidence retained for material decisions. 
 - Develop team capability in Physical Risk methodology, corporate structures and identifiers, GIS and mapping, asset materiality, SQL/BigQuery, QA, and relevant internal platforms. 
 - Create a collaborative learning environment through structured training, calibration sessions, knowledge sharing, and review of complex cases. 
Knowledge And Experience

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Geography, Geospatial Science, Environmental Science or Planning, Data Science, Engineering, or a related discipline. 
 - 6+ years of relevant experience in data operations related to geospatial or location data, GIS research, including experience leading people or project delivery. 
 - Demonstrated ability to manage priorities, resources, quality, and stakeholder expectations in a data-intensive operational environment. 
 - Working knowledge of corporate entity structures, asset-location data, geospatial concepts, mapping tools, and research-based verification. 
 - Proficiency in SQL, Python, and advanced Excel; practical experience querying and analyzing large datasets. Experience with BigQuery is strongly preferred. 
 - Strong analytical judgment, attention to detail, documentation discipline, and ability to resolve ambiguous or conflicting evidence. 
 - Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to present status, risks, recommendations, and decisions to technical and non-technical stakeholders. 

Preferred Knowledge And Experience

- Experience supporting Physical Risk, climate risk, catastrophe modelling, asset-level analytics, or commercial geospatial data products. 
 - Exposure to facility materiality, industrial assets, mines, utilities, damage-function or historical-loss research, and third-party location datasets. 
 - Experience with Power BI or similar reporting tools, workflow automation, and AI-assisted research or validation processes. 
 - Familiarity with data governance, audit controls, client data samples, and cross-functional product delivery.

data.title: Head of Payments Platform(Singapore)
data.description:
Job Summary

This role could be based in Singapore and India. When you start the application process you will be presented with a drop down menu showing all countries, Please ensure that you select a country where the role is based. 

Head of Payments Platforms will be the chief engineer and leader for Standard Chartered's core payment engines. He/she will lead an engineering division of engineers responsible for building, modernising, and scaling high-availability, high-throughput payment execution engines across our global footprint, ensuring uninterrupted operations within strict regulatory resilience frameworks. This end-to-end responsibility includes core engines, direct debits, clearing gateways, adaptors, global routers, and integration services. 

- Core Execution Architecture: Drive the technical vision, scale, and performance for core clearing engines, high-concurrency payment gateways, real-time transaction processing systems, and automated ledger entries. 
 - Corridor Scale & Latency: Engineer resilient, idempotent, low-latency execution engines capable of processing millions of cross-border and domestic payments daily across complex G-SIB corridors within critical cut off schedules and payment windows. 
 - Resilience, SRE & Telemetry: Guarantee maximum operational stability, near-zero downtime, and fault tolerance across execution pipelines. Own global transaction telemetry, and adherence to regulatory resilience standards (e. g. , DORA, CPS 230) and strict RTO targets. 
 - Legacy Modernisation: Lead the architectural evolution from legacy transaction engines to modern, distributed engines without impacting live payment corridors. 
 - People Management: Direct, mentor, and scale an engineering organisation of engineers. 

Key Responsibilities

Strategy

- Execute the Payments technology strategy defined by the CIO Payments and translate it into an actionable platform engineering roadmap. 
 - Define and continuously evolve the target-state architecture for core payment execution capabilities, including transaction processing, clearing, settlement, payment gateways and ledger platforms. 
 - Drive modernization of payment transaction engines, messaging layers, workflow orchestration and execution services while ensuring uninterrupted client and business operations. 
 - Lead engineering decisions that improve scalability, resilience, performance, security and maintainability of the Payments platform estate. 
 - Partner with Architecture, Engineering and Product stakeholders to ensure platform designs align with the broader Payments and enterprise technology strategy. 
 - Develop technology roadmaps for platform simplification, technical debt reduction, observability, automation and resilience improvements. 
 - Identify emerging technology opportunities and engineering innovations that support future payment volumes, new payment schemes and evolving client requirements. 

Business

- Deliver and operate the strategic payment platform capabilities required to support the Bank's domestic, cross-border and real-time payments business. 
 - Partner with Transaction Banking, Cash Operations, Product, Architecture and Engineering teams to ensure platform capabilities support business growth and client outcomes. 
 - Own platform performance, transaction throughput, latency, availability and service quality across critical payment corridors. 
 - Support delivery of new payment products, market initiatives, regulatory changes and payment network requirements. 
 - Lead engineering execution for strategic payments programmes, market migrations and platform consolidation initiatives. 
 - Ensure platform capabilities support operational efficiency, straight-through-processing, resiliency and improved client experience. 
 - Provide technology leadership and subject matter expertise across payment execution, processing and settlement capabilities. 

Processes

- Lead engineering, development, platform operations and service management processes across the Payments Platform estate. 
 - Establish engineering excellence standards covering software development lifecycle, DevSecOps, Site Reliability Engineering, testing, release management and platform operations. 
 - Ensure payment platforms are engineered for high throughput, low latency, idempotency and resilience across critical domestic and international payment corridors. 
 - Implement automated deployment, testing, monitoring, recovery and support processes to improve operational efficiency and reduce risk. 
 - Drive continuous improvement of payment execution, reconciliation, settlement and exception management processes. 
 - Lead management of platform dependencies, technology lifecycle activities and vendor-supported services. 
 - Support the Bank's product operating model through effective alignment of Build and Run teams across the platform lifecycle. 

People & Talent

- Build and lead a high-performing global engineering, platform and site reliability organisation supporting the Payments Platform estate. 
 - Create a culture of engineering excellence, accountability, innovation, ownership and continuous improvement. 
 - Develop organisational capability across distributed systems engineering, cloud technologies, payments processing, resilience engineering and platform operations. 
 - Attract, retain and develop world-class engineering talent through effective succession planning, career development and capability-building initiatives. 
 - Coach and mentor engineering leaders and senior technical contributors. 
 - Establish clear performance expectations, engineering standards and measurable delivery outcomes. 
 - Promote agile ways of working, inclusion, collaboration and continuous learning across global teams. 

Risk Management

- Own technology and operational risk management for the Payments Platform estate. 
 - Ensure payment platforms comply with regulatory resilience and operational risk requirements, including DORA, CPS 230 and applicable payment scheme obligations. 
 - Maintain strong controls around platform availability, recoverability, cyber resilience, secure development and technology lifecycle management. 
 - Lead identification, remediation and escalation of platform risks, vulnerabilities and control weaknesses. 
 - Ensure recovery strategies, disaster recovery capabilities and business continuity arrangements meet agreed recovery objectives. 
 - Drive proactive incident prevention through observability, telemetry, capacity management and resilience engineering practices. 
 - Partner with Risk, Compliance, Cyber Security and Audit stakeholders to maintain an effective control environment across the platform estate. 

Governance

- Operate governance frameworks that ensure the Payments Platform estate meets enterprise architecture, engineering, security and operational standards. 
 - Provide regular reporting on platform health, resilience, transformation progress, risks, technical debt and investment outcomes to the CIO Payments and governance forums. 
 - Ensure platform decisions comply with approved architecture standards, engineering controls, technology policies and regulatory requirements. 
 - Lead platform review forums covering resilience, service performance, operational risk, capacity management and modernization initiatives. 
 - Maintain effective oversight of third-party technology partners and platform service providers. 
 - Support internal and external audits, regulatory reviews and remediation activities. 
 - Promote the Group's values, Code of Conduct and risk culture across the Payments Platform organisation. 

Regulatory & Business Conduct

- Display exemplary conduct and live by the Group's Values and Code of Conduct. 
 - Take personal responsibility for embedding the highest standards of ethics, including regulatory and business conduct, across Standard Chartered Bank. This includes understanding and ensuring compliance with, in letter and spirit, all applicable laws, regulations, guidelines and the Group Code of Conduct. 
 - Effectively and collaboratively identify, escalate, mitigate and resolve risk, conduct and compliance matters. 

Key stakeholders

- Business Leaders (TB Cash and Payments)
 - Country CIOs / CTOs, T&O Leadership
 - Payments Product Management
 - Engineering, Infrastructure & Platform Teams
 - Enterprise Architecture
 - Cyber Security / ICS
 - Programme & Change Delivery Teams
 - Operations & Service Resilience Teams

Other Responsibilities

- Embed Here for good and Group's brand and values in Payments Platform. Perform other responsibilities assigned under Group, Country, Business or Functional policies and procedures. 

Skills And Experience

- Operational Risk Control
 - Software Engineering
 - Distributed Systems
 - Transaction Banking Processes
 - Payment Gateways
 - Clearing Engine
 - Message Transformation

Our Ideal Candidate

- Deep expertise in software engineering, distributed systems, and low-latency transaction processing in transaction banking. 
 - Mastery of high-throughput payment gateways, clearing engine design, message transformation, and ledger integration. 
 - Proven track record of maintaining high-availability SLAs, payment resilience, and regulatory operational risk controls within strict operational schedules. 
 - Experience leading engineering organizations of ~80+ headcount in a global bank or high-scale fintech. 

About Standard Chartered

We're a global bank connecting clients to our differentiated network, offering growth opportunities in the world's most dynamic markets. Our strategy, which combines cross-border capabilities and leading wealth management expertise, helps us deliver our purpose - to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity. 

Over our 170-year history, and across a unique geographical footprint connecting Asia, Africa and the Middle East to each other and the world, we've built a bank like no other, with diverse capabilities and partnerships that set us apart. 

What We Offer

- Being part of an inclusive and values driven organisation, one that embraces and celebrates our unique diversity, across our teams, business functions, and geographies. 
 - In line with our Fair Pay Charter, we offer a competitive salary and benefits to support your mental, physical, financial and social wellbeing. 
 - Core bank funding for retirement savings, medical and life insurance, with flexible and voluntary benefits available in some locations. 
 - Time-off including annual leave, parental/maternity (20 weeks), sabbatical (12 months maximum) and volunteering leave (3 days), along with minimum global standards for annual and public holiday, which is combined to 30 days minimum. 
 - Flexible working options based around home and office locations, with flexible working patterns. 
 - Proactive wellbeing support through Unmind, a market-leading digital wellbeing platform, development courses for resilience and other human skills, global employee assistance programme, sick leave, mental health first-aiders and self-help toolkits. 
 - A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual, and digital learning. 

Visit our careers website to learn more about us: www. sc. com/careers. 

Recruitment Assessments

Some of our roles use assessments to help us understand how suitable you are for the role you've applied to. If you are invited to take an assessment, this is great news. It means your application has progressed to an important stage of our recruitment process.

data.title: Solution Architect - AWS Integration & API Gateway
data.description:
Job Description

We are seeking a Solution Architect to design and lead a central email gateway. It will sit between the client's commerce platform, its middleware (enterprise service bus) and a new email service provider, and will carry all business-critical transactional email, such as order, shipping, refund and account notifications. The gateway offers two integration models: 

- a pass-through API for systems that are ready to use the new provider directly
 - a backward-compatible API that mimics the legacy provider, so existing systems only need to change an endpoint

The Architect will own the AWS target architecture, the versioned API contracts, a configuration-driven mapping model, and the resilience design needed to make sure no email is lost or sent twice. The role leads a small cross-functional team on a short build window, drives technical decisions with the client's architects, and owns cutover readiness and early-life support. 

Responsibilities

Architecture & Design

- Own the AWS target architecture across edge, API Gateway, private networking, load-balancing and ECS Fargate integration, containerized compute, eventing, audit and data flows
 - Define versioned OpenAPI contracts for the pass-through and backward-compatible APIs
 - Design a configuration-driven mapping engine for campaign, field and error-code translation
 - Design resilience patterns: timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breaker, idempotency and dead-letter queue (DLQ) handling
 - Design the Security & Observability Framework

Technical Leadership

- Lead discovery and capture existing integration contracts from live traffic
 - Set engineering standards and review all code, including AI-generated code
 - Guide developers, DevOps and QA on design, testability and performance
 - Establish AI-assisted application-building workflows using AI approved

Stakeholder & Delivery

- Present options and recommendations to the client's architecture and platform teams
 - Coordinate the ecommerce, middleware and email provider teams through integration and SIT
 - Own cutover planning, go/no-go criteria and early-life support

Security & Compliance

- Ensure OAuth2 machine-to-machine authentication, encryption, least-privilege IAM and PII masking
 - Align audit retention and the data purge approach with GDPR/CCPA requirements

Qualifications

Required Skills & Competencies

- Strong solution architecture experience on AWS: API Gateway, ECS/Fargate, SQS, EventBridge, Secrets Manager, IAM and KMS 
 - Configuration management using AppConfig or DynamoDB; observability with CloudWatch and OpenTelemetry/ADOT or X-Ray; CI/CD and infrastructure-as-code design. 
 - Proven design of API gateways or enterprise integration layers for high-volume transactional systems
 - Hands-on with Node. js/TypeScript or Java/Spring Boot microservices
 - Strong grasp of resilience patterns, idempotency and event-driven design
 - OpenAPI-first design and contract testing practices
 - Excellent stakeholder communication and technical leadership

Good-to-Have

- Exposure to email service provider platforms; retail transactional email, ESB/middleware platforms
 - Fastify; Akamai WAF; Terraform or AWS CDK; OpenSearch/ELK-based operational search. 
 - AWS Solutions Architect - Professional certification

Qualifications

- 12+ years of relevant software engineering experience with solution architecture and hands-on technical leadership. 
 - B. E. /B. Tech/MCA or equivalent
 - AWS architecture certification is desirable.

Part of the $4. 8 billion RPG Group, we're a community of 10, 000+ innovators across 30+ global locations, including Milpitas, Seattle, Princeton, Cape Town, London, Zurich, Singapore, and Mexico City. data.title: Senior Software Architect
data.description:
About SBS

SBS is a global financial technology company and an independently operated portfolio company of 74Software, an enterprise software group focused on mission-critical products and durable customer outcomes. SBS provides composable, cloud-based software across banking, lending, compliance, payments, consumer and asset finance. This role sits within the SBS India engineering team in Noida and contributes directly to the evolution of Digital Core and Payments. 

Role Summary

We are seeking a highly experienced, hands-on Senior Software Architect to shape SBS Digital Core, a strategic product AI Native Core Banking System spanning account and deposit management, product and pricing, payment processing and financial-crime controls. This is a senior technical leadership role, but not a hands-off advisory role: you will be expected to guide architecture, reduce technical debt, coach engineers and still personally produce deliverable engineering outcomes using modern tools, including approved AI coding assistants such as Claude, Codex and comparable enterprise-approved models. You will combine banking-domain depth, product architecture and hands-on engineering to turn complex banking, payments, regulatory and operational requirements into reusable, cloud-native capabilities incl. AI Use cases. The mandate is to build differentiated software that can scale across customers, markets and deployment models while enabling banks to modernise progressively. 

AI is part of the engineering method: use approved frontier and code-generation models such as Claude, Codex and comparable enterprise tools to accelerate architecture exploration, solution design, coding, testing and documentation. The expectation is not only to recommend direction, but to convert that direction into reviewed code, reference implementations, tests, migration patterns and working technical assets, while retaining human accountability, security controls and rigorous review. 

Why This Role Matters

Build a strategic growth platform. Digital Core sit at the centre of SBS's move towards AI native modular products, SaaS expansion and a more recurring, scalable software model. Your work will help protect trusted customer relationships while creating reusable capabilities for new growth. 

Engineer mission-critical banking. Shape the systems that manage accounts, deposits, product and pricing rules, real-time transactions and the full payment lifecycle, where availability, correctness, security and auditability are non-negotiable while providing AI capabilities to our customers

Create reusable product value. Design capabilities once and make them reusable across markets, deployment models and SBS products, reducing duplication while accelerating customer outcomes. 

Turn the digital core into an intelligent core. Embed governed AI, real-time data and automation into core operations so banks can improve decisions, service and operational efficiency without sacrificing deterministic controls. 

Influence a visible transformation. Work where product strategy, R&D focus, early-adopter delivery and engineering execution meet. Your architectural decisions will shape a flagship platform within SBS . 

Key Responsibilities

Architect distributed platforms. Design high-availability, cloud-native SaaS solutions using microservices, event-driven architecture and well-defined domain boundaries. 

Lead hands-on engineering. Write and review production code, reference implementations and reusable components for secure, resilient and maintainable services. 

Apply AI-assisted engineering. Use the latest approved AI models and coding assistants to produce and compare design options, draft architecture decision records, generate and refactor code, create tests, explain legacy code and improve technical documentation. 

Engineer responsibly with AI. Define prompts, context, evaluation criteria and review gates. Validate generated outputs for correctness, security, performance, licensing, privacy, bias and maintainability. Never expose confidential data to unapproved services. 

Convert architecture into deliverables. Personally produce hands-on outputs such as prototype services, reference implementations, proof points, migration utilities, test suites, performance experiments, code reviews and technical documentation that teams can adopt directly. 

Own banking-domain architecture. Translate the semantics and controls of deposits, account management, product and pricing, payment processing, into clear domain models, APIs, events and invariants

Enable progressive modernisation. Design coexistence and migration patterns that allow banks to introduce modular capabilities, run new and legacy services side by side and move products and customers at a controlled pace. 

Own non-functional architecture. Drive performance, scalability, availability, observability, recoverability, maintainability and security from design through production. 

Shape cloud-native delivery. Leverage Kubernetes and AWS services; guide containerisation, deployment topology, configuration, secrets and release patterns. 

Embed quality and DevSecOps. Promote TDD, contract testing, automated quality controls, threat modelling and efficient CI/CD practices. 

Influence technical direction. Define and challenge application design strategies, standards, guardrails and effective development workflows. 

Collaborate and communicate. Work with product, business, security, architecture and engineering stakeholders, and present complex decisions clearly. 

Lead technical change management. Help teams adapt to AI-assisted engineering and modern delivery practices by setting examples, creating guardrails, running enablement sessions and building confidence in new ways of working. 

Build a strong technical bench. Raise the engineering bar through hiring input, interviewing, coaching, mentoring and succession planning, creating a team of strong technical people around the role rather than becoming a single point of dependency. 

Core Technical Skills

Backend engineering: Expert-level Java, including modern Java versions and strong Spring Boot experience; reactive programming and Spring WebFlux are advantageous. 

Architecture: Distributed systems, Domain-Driven Design, Event-Driven Architecture, microservices, APIs and SaaS product architecture. 

Data and messaging: SQL and NoSQL technologies such as PostgreSQL, MongoDB and Redis; event streaming with Kafka. 

Cloud and platform: AWS, Kubernetes, Docker and Helm; GitLab CI and Argo CD experience is valuable. 

Quality engineering: JUnit, TDD, Spring Cloud Contract, automated integration and performance testing; K6 experience is advantageous. 

Front end and data processing: Working knowledge of TypeScript and Angular; Apache Spark exposure is beneficial. 

Security and compliance: Secure-by-design architecture, threat modelling, identity, data protection and financial-services regulatory expectations. 

AI engineering: Practical experience with enterprise-approved generative AI and coding assistants for architecture, code and test generation; ability to evaluate model outputs and design safe human-in-the-loop workflows. 

Hands-on delivery credibility: Proven record of remaining close to code and delivery while operating at senior architect level; comfortable producing tangible engineering assets rather than limiting contribution to strategy, reviews or governance. 

Qualifications

Experience: 10+ years in software engineering within large product teams, including 5+ years of hands-on design responsibility for complex distributed solutions. 

Education: Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience. 

Leadership: Demonstrated ability to lead technical teams, influence decisions, resolve complex architectural challenges and communicate with senior stakeholders while staying close enough to implementation to unblock delivery and model excellent engineering practice. 

Domain: Experience in fintech, banking or payments, with an understanding of financial-sector security and compliance. 

AI fluency: Evidence of using modern AI models to improve architecture and engineering outcomes, combined with disciplined verification, secure data handling and measurable quality controls. 

Change agent: Experience helping engineering teams adopt new tools, AI-assisted workflows, modern development practices and higher standards through coaching, hands-on examples and pragmatic guardrails. 

Mindset: Curiosity, sound judgement, continuous learning and a track record of introducing valuable technology without compromising product quality. 

What Drives Our Teams

We build mission-critical software with a long-term product mindset. Digital Core combines the scale and rigour of core banking with the pace of a modern software platform: modular architecture, API-first integration, real-time processing, cloud-native delivery, deep regulatory awareness and responsible AI. Architects are expected to contribute directly to code and design, simplify complexity, create reusable capabilities, coach others into stronger engineering habits and lead the change towards AI-enabled ways of working that improve customer outcomes across markets.

data.title: Builder QA II
data.description:
Job Description

You are an engineer who specialises in proving things work. The distinction between "dev" and "QA" work is not one we maintain: you read the application code, you write production-grade Python, and you build agents. The difference is what you point them at. 

- Core DNA
 - AI-Native Workflow. You use AI to accelerate everything you do as a default, not an experiment. You have opinions about which tools earn their place. 
 - Agentic Implementation. You build, debug and deploy autonomous agents - LLM-driven test generation, Playwright browser-use agents, self-healing locator strategies - against complex ERP screens and workflows. 
 - Legacy-to-Modern Bridge. Some of what you'll test is a modern web rewrite. Some is a desktop application older than your career. Both are puzzles. 
 - Evidence Over Confidence. A generated test that has never been executed is not a test. You know your own false-positive and flake rates rather than claiming there aren't any. 
 - What You Own

The ticket-to-test pipeline. An agent that reads a requirement or defect, understands the affected area, and produces a real test - grounded in the actual application, not in what the model imagines the application looks like. Hallucinated locators are the failure mode that kills these systems; preventing them is your problem. 

Execution and stabilization. Generation is the easy half. Your pipeline isn't done when a test file exists or a ticket gets created - it's done when the test has run against a real build, passed repeatedly, and earned its place in the suite. Flake is the enemy, because a suite nobody trusts is worse than no suite. 

Coverage that means something. You can tell the difference between a suite that covers the code and a suite that covers the risk. You use mutation testing and real defect history rather than counting tests, and you argue for the edge cases that actually bite: fiscal calendars, multi-currency, partial shipments, period-end adjustments. 

- Where You Might Lean In
 - Test Generation & Grounding - the retrieval and context problem. How does an agent know what the screen really contains, what the business rule really is, and what changed in this release? 
 - Adversarial & Red-Team - you build agents whose job is to break things. Programmatic prompt optimization (DSPy), fuzzing business logic, hunting the input nobody thought of. 
 - Test Infrastructure & Agent-Ops - the factory the test agents run in: parallel execution, environment and data management, tracing, and the observability to know why a run went sideways. 
 - Legacy Surface Automation - desktop and thick-client applications where modern tooling doesn't reach and the automation has to be built rather than installed. 

What You'll Actually Do

- Build test-generation agents that take a ticket and produce an executable test grounded in the live application. 
 - Close the loop. Make generation, execution, stabilization and reporting one pipeline rather than four disconnected steps with a human carrying work between them. 
 - Automate the untestable. Wrap legacy business logic - the modules everyone has avoided because there's no spec - in characterization tests that capture what the system actually does today. 
 - Kill flake. Find the root cause rather than adding a retry. Retries are how suites die. 
 - Red-team the financial logic. Build the agents that go looking for the case where the ledger doesn't balance. 
 - Fix your own agents in production. Read the traces, find why it went sideways, make it not happen again. 

What Good Looks Like

(Illustrative - real targets agreed with the hiring manager. )

- 30 days: Shipped your first agent-generated test into a running suite - generated, executed, stable. 
 - 90 days: Owning the ticket-to-test pipeline for a product area end to end, with a measured flake rate and a real coverage picture. 
 - 6 months: Other Builders reuse what you built. Escaped defects in your area are measurably down, and you can show why. 

The Stack

Python, pytest, Playwright, SQL (Postgres/SQL Server), TypeScript, OpenAI/Anthropic, LangChain/LangGraph, DSPy, pgvector/Qdrant, Docker, CI/CD pipelines, OpenTelemetry, eval and tracing platforms (LangSmith / Langfuse / Braintrust or equivalent), desktop automation frameworks where the application demands it. And any other tool that helps us achieve greatness. 

Who You Are

- You've shipped one. You have built at least one autonomous agent or complex LLM workflow that real people used for real work - not a weekend demo. You know how it failed, because it did. 
 - You write real code. Python that goes to production and gets reviewed like anyone else's. If your automation experience stops at a record-and-playback tool, this isn't the role. 
 - The manual-task hater. You have a physical reaction to repetitive work. If you do it twice, you've already started drafting the automation. 
 - Technically fearless. A 500-table undocumented legacy schema isn't complexity, it's a puzzle about to get solved. You aren't intimidated by spaghetti code - you're the one who brings the sauce. 
 - Rigor over hype. You love the new models and you still ask for the numbers. You know the difference between a cool demo and a pipeline people rely on every release. 
 - Suspicious by instinct. Your first question about any green build is what it didn't check. 

Why Join Us

- Quality is engineering here, not a stage gate. You are a Builder on the same ladder, with the same levels and the same expectations as everyone else in the squad. You build; you don't sign off on other people's work. 
 - The Final Boss of complexity. ERPs are the ultimate challenge for AI. If you can build agents that validate a General Ledger, you've solved the hardest version of this problem. 
 - Agentic autonomy. We don't do tickets. We do missions. You'll have real freedom over the models, frameworks and agent architectures you think will win. 
 - No red tape. If the agent works and the evals pass, we ship. No Change Management Committee - a "Does It Work?" policy. 
 - The Builder Tribe. You won't be the only AI person in the room. You'll be part of a small squad equally obsessed with moving faster, where your automation hacks are your biggest contribution rather than a hidden side project.

- Integrate automated test suites into CI/CD pipelines using Jenkins, GitLab or Azure DevOps to enable continuous testing. 
 - Maintain and refactor automation assets in response to thick clients version upgrades, configuration changes and screen changes.

Documentation & Collaboration: 

- Prepare and maintain test strategy, automation approach, test plans, test scenarios, scripts and requirement traceability matrices.

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible. 

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution - then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

Job Description

As a Test Automation Engineer, you will design and implement automation solutions that validate system behavior across UI, APIs, and integrations. You will contribute to building a robust quality engineering ecosystem by integrating automated testing into CI/CD pipelines and supporting continuous delivery. 

In this role, you will translate requirements into effective test strategies, combining automation with manual, exploratory, and integration testing to ensure comprehensive quality coverage across all application layers. 

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys hands-on coding, solving complex validation challenges, and improving system quality at scale, while taking ownership of end-to-end quality outcomes and collaborating closely with cross-functional teams. 

Responsibilities

Automation Development & Framework Ownership

- Design, develop, and own scalable test automation frameworks and reusable components
 - Build automated test suites across: 
 - UI (Web/Mobile)
 - API and integration layers
 - Ensure automation solutions are maintainable, reliable, and extensible across teams

Test Strategy & Implementation

- Translate requirements into automation-ready test scenarios, test data, and validation strategies
 - Contribute to test strategy, coverage planning, and quality goals
 - Identify test gaps and proactively mitigate risks
 - Perform automation feasibility analysis to determine optimal test approach (manual vs automated)

Delivery & Execution Excellence

- Execute a balanced mix of automated and manual tests aligned with sprint goals, ensuring comprehensive validation across functional, integration, and edge-case scenarios. 
 - Contribute to task breakdown, estimation, and sprint commitments
 - Proactively raise risks, blockers, and testability concerns
 - Identify, log, prioritize, and track defects through resolution lifecycle
 - Perform root cause analysis and collaborate with development teams for fixes

Manual & Functional Testing

- Design, document, and execute detailed test cases and test scenarios
 - Perform functional, exploratory, and regression testing across features
 - Validate end-to-end workflows and business scenarios
 - Identify edge cases and usability issues through exploratory testing
 - Ensure test coverage for areas not suitable for automation

Quality, Standards & Engineering Practices

- Write clean, testable, and maintainable automation code
 - Participate in code reviews and continuous improvement of automation frameworks
 - Ensure adherence to Definition of Ready (DoR) and Definition of Done (DoD)
 - Take ownership of end-to-end quality outcomes across assigned areas
 - Follow established DevOps, security, and quality engineering practices

CI/CD & DevOps Integration

- Integrate automation into CI/CD pipelines (Azure DevOps preferred)
 - Enable continuous testing and shift-left quality practices
 - Monitor and improve pipeline stability, execution time, and reliability
 - Validate and troubleshoot system integrations, data flows, and error handling based on defined architectural designs and interfaces

Non-Functional Testing

- Contribute to performance, reliability, and resilience testing
 - Validate system behavior under load, stress, and failure scenarios

Observability & Debuggability

- Leverage logs, metrics, and traces to improve test reliability
 - Support root cause analysis of failures and improve system observability

Test Data & Environment Management

- Design and manage test data strategies and datasets
 - Ensure availability of stable, production-like test environments

Incident & Operational Support

- Assist in troubleshooting defects across environments
 - Support maintenance and continuous improvement of automation suites
 - Analyze and reduce flaky tests and unstable scenarios

Collaboration & Growth

- Collaborate with developers, QA, Product Owners, and Tech Leads
 - Actively learn and adopt new tools, frameworks, and best practices
 - Contribute to team knowledge sharing and a strong quality culture

Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in computer science, IT, or related field
 - 5+ years of experience in software testing with strong automation focus
 - Experience in designing and implementing test automation frameworks
 - Strong understanding of testing principles, SDLC, STLC, and Agile practices

Technical Skills

- Programming experience in one or more: C#, Java, Python, JavaScript, Swift
 - Experience with automation tools such as Selenium, Katalon, Playwright, Cypress
 - Experience with: 
 - API testing (REST, Postman, etc. )
 - Version control (Git)
 - CI/CD pipelines (Azure DevOps)
 - Familiarity with: 
 - Test data management
 - Test reporting and logging tools
 - Debugging and root cause analysis
 - Release Management
Assets

- Experience with: 
 - Performance testing tools (JMeter, k6)
 - Security testing (SAST, DAST, SCA)
 - Exposure to: 
 - Cloud platforms (Azure preferred)
 - DevSecOps practices
 - Experience using AI-assisted tools responsibly (e. g. , GitHub Copilot)
Key Expectations

- Drive an automation-first approach (target 60-80% regression automation), while ensuring critical flows and edge cases are validated through manual testing where automation is not feasible or cost-effective. 
 - Own and evolve automation frameworks and quality engineering practices
 - Ensure high reliability, scalability, and stability of automation pipelines
 - Take accountability for quality outcomes, not just test execution
 - Ensure alignment with organizational quality, security, and compliance standards

Why Husky?

- Regulated Working Hours: Enjoy a structured work schedule that promotes a healthy work-life balance, allowing you to excel professionally while maintaining personal well-being. 
 - Visible Impact: Experience the satisfaction of seeing the direct outcomes of your work, as you contribute to projects that visibly enhance our company's technological capabilities and efficiency. 
 - Strategic Influence: Participate in architectural and technical reviews, contributing to the strategic direction of our cloud initiatives and making a tangible impact on our company's technological landscape. 
 - Empowered Involvement: Take an active role in decision-making processes and architectural reviews, where your expertise helps shape the future of our cloud solutions and overall business strategy.

data.title: Vice President ML Ops Engineer
data.description:
Embark on a transformative journey as Vice President-ML Ops Engineer at Barclays, where you will play a pivotal role to manage operations within a business area and maintain processes with risk management initiatives. You will take ownership of your work and provide first-class support to our clients with expertise and care. 

Purpose Of The Role

To lead the design, implementation, and governance of enterprise-grade ML Ops frameworks that enable scalable, secure, and efficient deployment of AI and Generative AI models, while driving best practices in automation, monitoring, and AWS architecture. 

Accountabilities Are Given Below

- Lead and mentor a high‐performing ML Ops engineering team, driving ownership, skill development, and cross‐functional collaboration across Data Science, Engineering, Cloud, and Security. 
 - Architect and govern scalable, secure, and cost‐optimized AWS platforms (SageMaker, EKS, Lambda, Step Functions) for enterprise ML and GenAI workloads. 
 - Design and implement automated ML pipelines covering data ingestion, management, feature processing, and high‐throughput model training/inference workflows, ensuring reliable, low‐latency, production‐grade consumption patterns. 
 - Establish robust data and model governance frameworks, including quality checks, lineage, auditability, and regulatory compliance. 
 - Build comprehensive model observability and monitoring systems for performance, drift, data quality, latency, and operational health using CloudWatch and custom dashboards. 
 - Drive security, reliability, and operational excellence, ensuring strong IAM practices, encryption, secrets management, and cloud cost optimization. 

Technical Skills Required For This Role Include

- Experience in Programming & Automation: Python, Bash, SQL. 
 - MLOps Tools: MLflow, Kubeflow, AWS SageMaker Pipelines Cloud Platforms: AWS (SageMaker, Bedrock, Lambda, Step Functions, CloudWatch)

This role requires a flexible working approach, ensuring availability during select hours that overlap with US-based partners and stakeholders. 

You may be assessed on key essential skills relevant to succeed in role, such as risk and controls, change and transformation, business acumen, strategic thinking and digital and technology, as well as job-specific technical skills. 

This role is based out of Noida.

To develop and lead the execution of business unit/function data strategy, ensuring the effective and efficient use of data to drive informed decision-making, support regulatory and control requirements, improve operational efficiency, and generate business value. 

Accountabilities

- Definition and oversight of data governance and procedures to address control and regulatory requirements, including Data Privacy. 
 - Definition and oversight of data analytics and insights that support the effective management of the business and well as driving commercial outcomes. 
 - Development of a team of data professionals with expertise in data analytics, data engineering, data science, and other relevant disciplines. 
 - Analysis of the bank's current data landscape, identify key data assets and gaps, and develop a roadmap for future data initiatives. 
 - Monitoring team performance and setting clear performance expectations.

- To contribute or set strategy, drive requirements and make recommendations for change. Plan resources, budgets, and policies; manage and maintain policies/ processes; deliver continuous improvements and escalate breaches of policies/procedures. .

They may also lead a number of specialists to influence the operations of a department, in alignment with strategic as well as tactical priorities, while balancing short and long term goals and ensuring that budgets and schedules meet corporate requirements. .

The four LEAD behaviours are: L - Listen and be authentic, E - Energise and inspire, A - Align across the enterprise, D - Develop others. . 
 - OR for an individual contributor, they will be a subject matter expert within own discipline and will guide technical direction. They will lead collaborative, multi-year assignments and guide team members through structured assignments, identify the need for the inclusion of other areas of specialisation to complete assignments. They will train, guide and coach less experienced specialists and provide information affecting long term profits, organisational risks and strategic decisions. . 
 - Advise key stakeholders, including functional leadership teams and senior management on functional and cross functional areas of impact and alignment. 
 - Manage and mitigate risks through assessment, in support of the control and governance agenda. 
 - Demonstrate leadership and accountability for managing risk and strengthening controls in relation to the work your team does. 
 - Demonstrate comprehensive understanding of the organisation functions to contribute to achieving the goals of the business. 
 - Collaborate with other areas of work, for business aligned support areas to keep up to speed with business activity and the business strategies. 
 - Create solutions based on sophisticated analytical thought comparing and selecting complex alternatives. In-depth analysis with interpretative thinking will be required to define problems and develop innovative solutions. 
 - Adopt and include the outcomes of extensive research in problem solving processes. 
 - Seek out, build and maintain trusting relationships and partnerships with internal and external stakeholders in order to accomplish key business objectives, using influencing and negotiating skills to achieve outcomes. 
 - The role is responsible for leading the design and governance of MLOps frameworks, AWS-based architectures, and automation strategies to enable efficient, secure, and scalable deployment of AI and Generative AI models

All colleagues will be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Values of Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence and Stewardship - our moral compass, helping us do what we believe is right. They will also be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Mindset - to Empower, Challenge and Drive - the operating manual for how we behave.
